speaker: will_kemp
text: You have had chances enough for an age to become official. I brought a gingerbread. It has suffered in the hat.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The font's day is the one my family can stand upon, though my mother holds by St George. I am not giving you a number to put in your mouth.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Whether celebrating twice obliges the company twice is the question, and I am asking it before anyone agrees.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: I am eating the corner. Agreement can catch me up.

speaker: will_kemp
text: You might have waited until the question was a question. The hat did what it could.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Let him eat. The day can stay unimportant. I am not standing on two ages.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Then answer the question while you chew, or leave it as a question. Twice is two occasions. I do not know that the company owes two.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: I owe this corner. I do not owe a speech. The afternoon's faults can stay in the afternoon.

speaker: will_kemp
text: I was not offering a fault. I was offering cake. You are welcome to be official, or you are welcome to be unfinished. The cake is the same cake.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Unfinished, then. My mother has her day. The font has this one. I am not making the company pay for either.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Good. One cake is not a second reckoning. The book is already shut.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: And the corner is already gone. I am not apologising to a hat.

speaker: will_kemp
text: The hat will recover. You will not get a second cake out of me to prove a point about twice.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I do not want a second cake. One is the joke, and the joke is enough.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Then the company is obliged once, by the cake, and not by the book. I can live with that.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Live with it quietly. My mouth is full, and the day is getting smaller, which is what we wanted.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Smaller is a compliment. I have made larger exits.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then make a small one. Thank you for the cake. I am not official, and I am not displeased.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Noted. No second line in the book. No second cake. We can go.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Go, then. Leave the crumbs for the chest, not for a speech.

speaker: will_kemp
text: The chest can have what the hat began. Four hands, if anyone is still interested in a picture of a sweet.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Four hands, and then home. The day is pleasantly unimportant. I intend to leave it so.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Unimportant, and shut. That is a good Saturday.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: I have had the corner. I am satisfied.

speaker: will_kemp
text: You are easily satisfied. Come away before I find another cake and ruin the arithmetic.
